fruits_veggies.title: Fruits & Vegetables: The Fresh Kitchen Guide
fruits_veggies.text: A complete everyday guide to fresh fruits and vegetables: choosing ripe produce, optimal kitchen storage, and bringing out vibrant flavors.

items.title: Fresh Avocados
items.text: Check firmness near the stem. Mash with lime juice, minced garlic, and sea salt for guacamole, slice over crusty sourdough toast, or blend into creamy smoothies.

items.title: Apples & Bananas
items.text: Apples provide dietary fiber and vitamin C; keep chilled to stay crisp. Bananas offer potassium and quick natural energy for workouts and morning oats.

items.title: Heirloom & Cherry Tomatoes
items.text: Store at room temperature to protect natural sweetness. Slow-roast cherry tomatoes with olive oil and garlic for pasta, or slice heirlooms with mozzarella and fresh basil.

items.title: Spinach & Leafy Greens
items.text: Keep dry in the crisper drawer lined with a paper towel. Flash-sauté with garlic and chili flakes, fold into morning eggs, or toss raw into fresh grain bowls.

items.title: Strawberries & Blueberries
items.text: Packed with antioxidants and flavonoids. Rinse in cold water just before eating to prevent moisture spoilage. Excellent in yogurts, rustic pastries, or fresh compotes.

items.title: Citrus (Lemons & Oranges)
items.text: Zest the peel before juicing to extract rich aromatic oils. Use bright acidity to balance rich sauces and vinaigrettes, or slice into ice water for daily refreshment.

items.title: Carrots & Sweet Potatoes
items.text: Rich in beta-carotene. Store in a cool, dark pantry away from moisture. Toss with olive oil, smoked paprika, and rosemary, then roast hot (400°F / 200°C) until caramelized.

items.title: Broccoli & Cruciferous Greens
items.text: Loaded with vitamins C and K plus folate. Steam lightly to keep vibrant color and crunch, or roast with shaved parmesan and red pepper flakes.
